I ran the light-collection simulation for all three permitted designs at 5%, 10%, 20% and 30% wall coverage, and recorded all 12 results.

| Design | 5% | 10% | 20% | 30% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Module-D1 | 12.5 | 22.9 | 36.4 | 51.4 |
| Module-D3 | 8.9 | 15.2 | 27.0 | 38.5 |
| Module-D2 | 5.7 | 10.5 | 16.7 | 24.0 |

(PE/MeV.)

Module-D1 gives the highest light collection at every coverage, and light collection rises with coverage for all three designs. At 30% coverage, the top of the allowed range, D1 reaches 51.4 PE/MeV.

The 20% values are close to the earlier 2025 summary (D1 36.4 vs 38, D3 27.0 vs 27, D2 16.7 vs 18).

Robustness is still unassessed. No project document excludes any design on robustness grounds, and this step did not test it. The bonded dichroic filter on D1 is a plausible fragility concern for a module that can't be accessed after filling, and that concern is unconfirmed. It matters for the final recommendation because D1 is the leader on light collection.
I'll re-check the documents for any cost or robustness trade-offs before comparing the designs, since earlier steps left robustness unresolved.
